question: Will the IOM Missing Migrants Project record at least 1,000 Mediterranean migrant deaths in 2026 before May 2026?
summary: 606 deaths by February 2026 imply a plausible path to 1,000 by end of May if early-2026 pace continues.
Adversarial objections point to downward pressure from policy/SAR restrictions, data-definition issues, and seasonal variability.
Data gaps and revisions could both inflate or deflate counts; historical volatility makes the trajectory uncertain.
Overall, adjust from ensemble toward a more conservative probability while preserving substantial chance.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid and indicate meaningful downward pressure on fatalities, though not determinative.
justification.adjustment: Applied a downward adjustment from the ensemble to 0.82 (range 0.72–0.92) to reflect the balance of upward pace with plausible reductions from policy/SAR, data revisions, and weather.

causal-factors.name: Spring weather/storm activity and SAR risk
causal-factors.rationale: Early 2026 disasters were associated with storms and rough seas; similar conditions in spring could sustain or raise fatality risk on central Mediterranean crossings.

synthesis: The early-2026 fatality pace makes hitting 1,000 by May plausible but uncertain. Objections indicate downward pressure from policy, data issues, and weather, warranting a tempered, calibrated probability below the raw ensemble.
